title.narrative: GICHD, Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining, 2025-2027
GICHD, Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining, 2025-2027

description.narrative:
Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining (GICHD) is an international expert organisation working to reduce the impacts of mines, cluster munition, and other explosive hazards in close partnership with national authorities, mine action organisations and other human security actors.
The GICHD aims to enhance expertise, methods and good practice of mine action, as well as develop innovative tools and technologies for clearance. Their work with Information Management helps national authorities and mine action organisations with the collection, analysis and timely provision of information to support clearance operations. On behalf of the United Nations, the GICHD also develops, maintains and promotes the International Mine Action Standards (IMAS). Furthermore, they work on promoting instruments of international law, norms and standards, and evidence-based policies. Advisory services and trainings on all aspects of mine action; institutional, strategic, managerial and operational, are provided, primarily for national authorities.
The contribution also includes a component with delegated funds from Sida's Ukraine strategy to strengthen the implementation of GICHD's country program in Ukraine. The program contributes, among other things, to the ongoing reform process of the institutional architecture for demining operations in the country, particularly to localization by strengthening the capacity of national demining organizations.

Geneva International Centre for Humanitarian Demining (GICHD) är en internationell expertorganisation som arbetar med att minska effekterna av minor, klusterammunition och andra explosiva ämnen i nära samarbete med nationella myndigheter, minhanteringsorganisationer och andra aktörer som arbetar med att främja mänsklig säkerhet.
GICHD arbetar med att öka expertis och förbättra metoder och verktyg inom röjning av minor och klusterammunition, samt att utveckla innovativa verktyg och teknologi för minhantering. Vidare arbetar de med informationshantering genom att hjälpa nationella myndigheter och minhanteringsorganisationer att samla, analysera och dela kunskap som stödjer minhanteringsinsatser på landnivå. GICHD har vidare fått mandat av FN att utgöra sekretariat för 'International Mine Action Standards' (IMAS). GICHD stöttar länder i deras efterlevande av internationell rätt och internationella standarder samt bidra till evidensdriven policyutveckling. GICHD erbjuder även utbildningar om de institutionella, strategiska och operationella dimensioner som är kopplade till minhantering, främst till nationella myndigheter.
Inom insatsen finns också en komponent med delegerade medel från Sidas Ukraina-strategi för att stärka upp genomförandet av GICHD:s landprogram i Ukraina. Programmet bidrar bl.a. till den reformeringsprocess av den institutionella arkitekturen för minröjningsoperationer som är på gång i landet och då särskilt till lokalisering genom att stärka kapaciteten hos nationella minröjningsorganisationer.

title.narrative: Beslut om ändring av insats GICHD 2025-2027

description.narrative:
Reporting for 2025, the first year under this agreement, has not yet been submitted. Results will thus be published within due time and in line with the agreement.
Results for 2024 have been reported, but belong to the previous agreement period. However, a few selected results are included here as well, meanwhile:
- In 2024, the GICHD launched the Innovation Hub, which plays a central role in this vision. It provides a platform for knowledge-sharing, connecting academics, tech experts, and practitioners to collaborate on practical evidence-based solutions based on concrete needs. In October 2024, the GICHD hosted an Innovation Session on artificial intelligence (AI) in Geneva. During this event, the first of its kind in the mine action sector, over 100 AI experts and mine action practitioners exchanged on challenges of the sector and possible ways to introduce AI in solutions. The event was a catalyst for several new funding proposals and projects within the sector, including a new project by the United Nations Office for Project Services (UNOPS) in South Sudan and one by the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Regional Mine Action Centre in Southeast Asia
Ukraine:
- The GICHD works with national authorities to ensure that capacities are enhanced, and in turn facilitating the safe, effective, and efficient implementation of operations. The guiding principles of innovation and sustainability underpin these effort. The GICHD e.g. delivered 7 training courses on mine action in Ukraine, including a tailored workshop. A key achievement towards enhancing national ownership sustainably was handing over to the government of Ukraine a tailored training management package for NTS and quality management. In Ukraine, the GICHD assessed the capacities of relevant state entities to advance gender equality and social inclusion in mine action response. Furthermore, the GICHD was invited to provide expert input to the OSCE Ministry of Economy of Ukraine workshop on gender in mine action.
- The GICHD undertook preparatory work for a new research initiative focused on the localisation of mine action in Ukraine. Activities included the mapping of relevant national and international mine action operators, conducting initial consultations to understand the operational landscape, and building connections with government stakeholders. This research will analyse the systemic factors, such as regulatory and policy frameworks and partnership modalities, that shape the environment for national operators in Ukraine. This work aligns with Sidas goal of promoting local ownership of national peace efforts
Women, Peace and Security:
- With the support of Sida, the GICHD is advancing its multi-country research to generate evidence on the linkages between the Women, Peace and Security (WPS) agenda and mine action. This research aims to demonstrate how gender-responsive mine action contributes to broader peace and security outcomes, and to provide practical guidance for integrating WPS commitments into mine action policy and practice across diverse contexts. Looking ahead, the GICHD will disseminate several key knowledge products by the end of 2025 to reinforce this work. These include a case study on Ukraine, a Recommendation Brief tailored for National Mine Action Authorities (NMAAs), and a second brief aimed at WPS stakeholders, highlighting practical entry points for integrating EORR within broader peace and security frameworks. In addition, the GICHD will organise a workshop in Colombia in late 2025 to engage youth in the ongoing Youth, Peace and Security (YPS) research process, helping to ensure their perspectives are reflected in future programming.
